name: Garrett Wilson

background.fact: Born July 22, 2000; Wikipedia says he was born in Chicago and grew up in Dublin, Ohio until age 11, while the ESPN and Sleeper data lists Austin, Texas as the birthplace.

He attended Lake Travis High School in Austin, Texas, won a 6A state title in 2016, set school receiving records (204 catches, 3,359 yards, 55 touchdowns) and played in the 2019 All-American Bowl as a five-star recruit.

At Ohio State he caught 30 passes for 432 yards and 5 touchdowns as a true freshman in 2019, moved to the slot in 2020, and became the second player in school history with four straight 100-yard games (Nov 21, 2020).
The Jets drafted him 10th overall in 2022 and he was named NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year.

scouts_read: Wilson is questionable with a concussion, but he practiced fully on Friday and coach Aaron Glenn said he is confident Wilson plays, so the main risk is a late scratch. If he plays, he is the clear top target for a Jets offense that has relied on Geno Smith for every pass, with about a quarter of all targets. Buffalo is a 7.5 point favorite, so the Jets may be chasing points, which helps his volume. His production has been uneven, from 2.6 to 16.7 points a game, and most of his catches are short. I would project a middling game of 8 to 12 points with a modest touchdown chance, and I would check the inactive list before kickoff.
